note: Adapted from entry 5, Odontotermes dives Hag. (1858), of Holmgren's Termitenstudien, originally in German; it is followed by entry 6, Odontotermes javanicus n. sp., so only the text of entry 5 is used. For the main form only the alate is known (the original states 'Soldaten und Arbeiter nicht bekannt'), and the soldier and worker are known only from Forma celebensis, which the original treats as a form of this species; it has been placed in the Other section with a note. OCR problems: the two columns of the measurement table (type specimens / alcohol specimens) were scrambled by OCR and have been restored according to the text; the head length of the Forma celebensis alate was OCR'd as 2.6«, the last digit being illegible, and is not recorded.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The body size of the alate varies greatly; because the size ranges overlap, it is difficult to separate it sharply from the very closely related O. grandiceps and O. celebensis. The 2 kinds of soldiers that Hagen at the time assigned to this species, together with the workers and juveniles mentioned at the same time, should belong to Termes and are unrelated to this species.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head chestnut brown, shining black in dried specimens; the base of the postclypeus, the anterior corners of the transverse band, antennae, mouthparts, a Y-shaped mark and two shoulder spots on the pronotum, the underside and the legs rusty yellow; the sides of the abdominal sternites light brown; wings grey (greyish yellow in alcohol), the costal margin brown. The head is covered with partly short hairs and partly longer setae, fairly densely; the body hairs are fairly dense; the wings bear several hairs towards the apex. Head broadly oval, narrowed anteriorly; frons slightly raised, not depressed; frontal gland distinctly raised and punctiform, with a weak longitudinal ridge extending forwards from it; the transverse band has 3 weak longitudinal grooves branching outwards; compound eyes medium-sized, projecting; ocelli medium-sized, their distance from the compound eye about its short diameter or slightly more, facing slightly laterally; the base of the postclypeus distinctly shorter than half its width, flatly convex, the posterior margin convex and the anterior margin slightly concave; antennae 19-segmented, segment 2 longer than segment 3, segment 3 as long as or slightly longer than segment 4. Pronotum relatively small, its anterior corners slightly projecting and strongly rounded, the lateral margins strongly convergent, the anterior margin slightly concave, the posterior emargination fairly deep; the mesonotal notch wider than that of the metanotum; the media sometimes forks at the middle with 5—6 branches, sometimes only in the last third with 2—3 branches; the cubitus has about 14—15 branches, mostly simple; 2—3 branches lie on the inner side of the origin of the media. Measurements (mm): body length with wings (type specimen) 26, (alcohol specimens) 21—28; body length without wings (type) 10, (alcohol) 12; forewing length 22—23; head length (type) 2.55—2.66, (alcohol) 2.60; head width (type) 2.28—2.47, (alcohol) 2.51—2.74; pronotal width (type) 2.2—2.34, (alcohol) 2.32—2.43; pronotal length (type) 1.06, (alcohol) 1.14.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Forma celebensis (given in the original as a form of this species): alate (wingless, Tafel IV, Fig. 10) very similar to the main form but slightly larger, the compound eyes larger and more projecting, the frontal gland less raised, the colour slightly darker, and the shape of the pronotum slightly different; measurements (mm): body length without wings 14; head width 2.62; pronotal width 2.43, length 1.14. Soldier (Tafel V, Fig. 8) much like the soldier of O. javanicus but with longer mandibles: head yellow, body whitish; head hairs sparse, body hairs not very dense; head oval, narrowed anteriorly, frontal gland invisible, the basal segment of the mandibles large, the base of the postclypeus small, the labrum ligulate, slightly pointed at the front, covering less than half of the mandibles; mandibles fairly long, slightly curved, the tooth of the left mandible small and situated in the anterior third, the right mandible toothless; antennae 17-segmented, segment 3 much shorter than segment 2 and slightly shorter than segment 4, segment 3 as long as segment 5; anterior margin of the pronotum notched. Measurements (mm): body length 7; head with mandibles 3.19, without mandibles 2.13; head width 1.71; pronotal width 1.18. Worker of two forms: head pale yellow, body whitish, pilosity fairly sparse; head quadrangular-rounded, frontal gland large and very distinct, the base of the postclypeus short and slightly raised; antennae 17-segmented in the small worker and 18-segmented in the large worker, segment 4 the shortest in the large form and segment 3 the shortest in the small form; anterior margin of the pronotum slightly concave. Measurements (mm): large worker body length 6, head width 1.67, pronotal width 0.87; small worker body length 4.5, head width 1.29, pronotal width 0.63.
